p0007.overview: Moab, the gateway to Arches and Canyonlands, hosts a modest food truck scene and a seasonal farmers' market. Visitors can find tacos, shaved ice, and wood-fired pizza at the Moab Food Truck Park. The Moab Farmers' Market adds local produce from late spring through fall.

blurbs.text: Late-night truck di pan vendors fire up their grills after 9 p.m., serving ribs, chicken sate, and fries drenched in peanut sauce. Mornings belong to snack shops frying pastechi—pastries filled with gouda or saltfish. The Local Market in Oranjestad features casual bites near the cruise terminal.

Local vendors around San Pedro de Atacama serve clay-oven empanadas and skewers of llama meat, while carts sell artisanal ice cream. In Calama, the Feria Modelo market supplies fresh Andean produce like native potatoes and quinoa.

p0063.overview: Street food centers on casual bites geared toward hikers and travelers. Empanadas, choripán (sausage sandwiches), and locro (a hearty stew) are common quick meals. Small local markets and bakeries supply provisions for the trails, especially during the summer hiking season.

blurbs.text: In summer, Bergen's Fisketorget is fully operational, with vendors selling fresh seafood, fish cakes, and sandwiches. Smaller coastal towns often host weekend markets or food festivals featuring local produce and traditional snacks like svele (pancakes).

Outdoor stalls thin out in the cold months. The focus shifts to indoor venues like Bergen's Mathallen (indoor food market), where visitors can still find local seafood, cured meats, and seasonal specialties like pinnekjøtt (cured lamb).

Los Kioskos on Charles Binford Avenue in Puerto Ayora is the main hub for street food. Every evening, the street is closed to traffic and filled with tables. Vendors grill fresh seafood, such as brujo (scorpionfish) and, from September to December, spiny lobster.

p0073.overview: Street food around Glacier and Waterton Lakes centers on summer farmers' markets in gateway towns like Whitefish and Columbia Falls. Visitors can find local specialties like huckleberry pastries, bison burgers, and fresh Flathead cherries at outdoor stalls.

p0076.overview: Gateway towns like Gatlinburg and Cherokee feature modest market eating. Visitors can find seasonal farmers markets selling Appalachian produce and baked goods, alongside permanent tourist stands serving funnel cakes and fudge.

p0077.overview: Greenland's market culture centers around the Brættet, local catch markets found in towns like Nuuk and Ilulissat. Hunters and fishermen bring daily hauls of seal, whale, reindeer, and fresh fish directly to these stalls.

blurbs.text: Heavy rains disrupt the open-air seafood stalls at Kampung Ujung, with vendors retreating under tarps. Pasar Wae Kesambi and other produce markets remain active, though street food carts are less frequent during downpours.

p0091.overview: Leh's Main Bazaar and nearby Tibetan markets form the center of Ladakh's street food scene. Pedestrian lanes hold stalls steaming with momos and bowls of thukpa or skyu, a traditional wheat pasta stew. Vendors also sell regional staples like chhurpi, a hard yak cheese, alongside cups of salty butter tea.

p0095.overview: The Lofoten Islands are not a major street food destination, but in summer, visitors can find harbor kiosks and seasonal markets serving local specialties like fiskekaker (fish cakes), stockfish snacks, and fresh fish burgers.

p0102.overview: Street food in the Maldives centers on Malé, where local markets and small stalls serve traditional snacks known as hedhikaa. Visitors can find fresh produce, dried fish, and short eats like bajiya and masroshi.

p0104.overview: Marlborough and the Abel Tasman area rely on weekend farmers' markets rather than daily street food stalls. Visitors find local produce, artisan cheeses, and hot food stalls at the Marlborough Farmers' Market in Blenheim and the Motueka Sunday Market near the national park. The warmer months bring the largest crowds and the widest variety of vendors.

p0110.overview: Fiordland is a remote wilderness, so street food is limited to the gateway town of Te Anau. Visitors can find a small number of food trucks serving casual bites like steamed buns or fish and chips. The warmer months bring the seasonal Te Anau Community Market.

p0111.overview: Mongolia's market eating centers on hearty, meat-heavy nomadic staples. In Ulaanbaatar, bazaars like Narantuul Market host stalls serving hot khuushuur (fried meat pastries) and suutei tsai (salty milk tea). The scene peaks in mid-summer when outdoor stalls multiply for festivals, featuring fresh dairy products like aaruul (dried curds) and steamed buuz dumplings.

p0114.overview: Namibia's street food scene centers on grilled meat over open fires. The most famous specialty is kapana, strips of beef grilled to order and dipped in chili salt, best experienced at Windhoek's Oshetu Community Market. Visitors will also find vetkoek and dried mopane worms.

p0137.overview: Papua New Guinea's food scene revolves around bustling open-air markets and casual kai bars. Visitors can find stalls selling roasted bananas, sweet potato (kaukau), and sago pudding (saksak), alongside fresh tropical fruits and smoked fish. Major hubs like Port Moresby's Koki Fish Market and the highland markets in Goroka and Mount Hagen feature the widest variety.

blurbs.text: During the high-water season, heavy rains can make open-air markets muddy and harder to navigate. The lower level of the Belén Market in Iquitos floods, and vendors move to higher ground or sell from canoes.

The low-water season brings easier access to markets and a wider variety of fresh produce. River fish are concentrated and plentiful at the stalls. This is the best time to explore the full extent of the Belén Market on foot.
Waisai's small market and harbor area host a few stalls selling grilled fish, satay, and fried rice. The focus is on basic Indonesian comfort food for locals and travelers passing through.

p0149.overview: Raja Ampat is a remote island group with a basic food scene. Street food is limited to small local markets and modest stalls in the main town of Waisai, with simple Indonesian staples like nasi goreng, mie goreng, and grilled fish.

p0164.overview: The Scottish Highlands and Isle of Skye feature a street food scene centered on fresh seafood and local game. Visitors find wooden shacks serving fresh langoustines and scallops right on the harbor in the warmer months, alongside monthly farmers' markets selling venison and haggis.

blurbs.text: The coastal seafood shacks operate at full capacity, serving fresh langoustines, crab, and oysters outdoors. Inverness Farmers' Market runs with its highest number of vendors selling local cheeses and venison.

p0165.overview: Sedona's small street food scene centers on the Sedona Community Farmers Market, with produce, tamales, and baked goods, and a winter schedule in the cooler months. A handful of food trucks operate around the city offering casual bites like tacos and Navajo fry bread.

p0199.overview: Visitors can find weekly farmers' markets selling Alpine cheeses and dried meats in valley towns, while winter brings roasted chestnut stands and holiday markets serving mulled wine. The best variety appears during the summer harvest and the December holiday season.

p0181.overview: Tierra del Fuego has a modest street food scene, with food trucks and local fairs in Ushuaia and Rio Grande. Visitors can find stalls serving choripán and baked empanadas. The scene is active in the warmer months when food trucks operate reliably near the ports.

p0159.overview: The town of Uyuni serves as the gateway to the salt flats, and visitors can explore Mercado Central for casual meals of llama meat or quinoa. Stalls around the town center sell baked salteñas in the morning and hot api with buñuelos in the evening.

p0197.overview: Yellowstone's gateway towns host modest summer farmers' markets. Visitors can find regional specialties like huckleberry preserves, elk jerky, and fresh produce at weekly outdoor stalls in West Yellowstone and Jackson.

blurbs.text: Summer rains bring fresh seasonal foods. Vendors roast fresh corn on the cob over charcoal, and macimbi (mopane worms) appear in the markets after the heavy showers.

p0193.overview: Victoria Falls and the surrounding towns feature modest local markets where visitors can try Zimbabwean staples. Open-air stalls and community hubs like Chinotimba Market host vendors selling roasted corn, dried kapenta, and seasonal macimbi.

p0200.overview: Street food in the national park gateway towns is limited to seasonal community gatherings like the Zion Canyon Farmers Market in Springdale, where vendors sell local produce, baked goods, and ready-to-eat snacks.
